baselines.note: Exactly the thresholds declared in configs/training.yaml and used on validation. No blind-optimal threshold was searched.

detection_delay.note: First-attempt detection is structurally weak by design: a first request is scored from prior attempts only, so a brand new device carries almost no evidence either way.

evidence_gate.note: Diagnostic only; the gate was not changed. A device counts as 'withheld' if some attempt scored at or above the (campaign adjusted) block threshold and the device was never blocked.

prevalence.note: Benchmark prevalence differs between validation and blind. PR-AUC is prevalence-dependent, so it is reported as benchmark PR-AUC and must not be read as a production precision estimate. Recall, FPR and the per-scenario rates carry the argument.

shift_characterisation: Blind v1.1 is a temporally held-out, composition-shifted, new-merchant synthetic benchmark with MODEST marginal feature-distribution shift (max PSI 0.115, 27/28 features below 0.10, median KS 0.032, minimum overlap 0.913). It is not a heavy covariate shift and must not be described as one.

validation_scenario_metrics.note: Development family names differ from blind family names by design, so these are read side by side rather than paired.
